description: nf-core/genomeassembler samplesheet context, aligned to the pinned 1.1.0 nextflow_schema.json and assets/schema_input.json. Assembly and scaffolding of haploid / unphased genomes from long reads.

flye.help: Flye is the default assembler and handles both ONT and HiFi input.

hifiasm.help: PacBio HiFi only. Turn on for a HiFi cohort; meaningless for Nanopore.

polish_medaka.help: Nanopore polishing. Not applicable to HiFi, which needs no polishing.

busco.help: Completeness scoring; downloads a lineage dataset on demand.

scaffold_ragtag.help: Reference-guided scaffolding; needs ref_fasta on the row.

pipeline.name: nf-core/genomeassembler
pipeline.core_rule: Columns are sample, ontreads, hifireads, ref_fasta, ref_gff, shortread_F, shortread_R, paired. Only `sample` is schema-required — because WHICH read column to fill depends on the sequencing platform. Nessie fills it per row from the platform recorded in the sample's own metadata: ontreads for Nanopore, hifireads for PacBio.
pipeline.reference_requirement: NONE for assembly — the 1.1.0 schema declares no genome/fasta/gtf. A per-row ref_fasta/ref_gff pair exists only for optional RagTag scaffolding against a related genome.

validation_rules: The read column is chosen by PLATFORM, not by read number. Nanopore reads go in ontreads; PacBio HiFi reads go in hifireads. Nessie derives this per row from the sample's metadata rather than asking, because the metadata is available earlier and is more reliable than a remembered answer.

A SHORT-READ-ONLY cohort is not a valid input. This is a long-read assembler; shortread_F/shortread_R exist only to polish a long-read assembly. If the platform resolves to Illumina the reads land in no recognised column and the row will be visibly empty — that is deliberate, not a bug. Stop and tell the user.

If the platform cannot be determined from metadata, every read column stays blank. Do not guess: ONT and HiFi have opposite error profiles and assembling one as the other silently degrades the result.
Do NOT pass --genome, --fasta or --gtf: the 1.1.0 schema declares none of them.
hifiasm is HiFi-only and polish_medaka is Nanopore-only. Setting either for the wrong platform wastes cluster time at best.
This assembles HAPLOID / unphased genomes. A diploid organism needs a phasing-aware assembler instead.
notes: NO MATCHING DATA IN NExtSEEK as of 2026-08-05: zero of 2,057 D.SEQ records are long-read on any platform. Catalogued so the capability exists when long-read data is registered. This pipeline is the reason the emitter grew PIPELINE_PLATFORM_COLUMNS: it was initially rejected because a platform-dependent column name could not be produced by the static alias map, and elicitation happens in configure_run, which runs AFTER write_samplesheet. Deriving the platform from the sample's own metadata solves it earlier and better.

sources.label: nf-core/genomeassembler nextflow_schema.json @ 1.1.0
sources.notes: Authoritative: no required params beyond input/outdir; no genome/fasta/gtf.

samplesheet_columns.description: Column-level field dictionary for the nf-core/genomeassembler input sheet.

ontreads.validation_hints: Filled automatically when the sample's metadata says Nanopore.

hifireads.validation_hints: Filled automatically when the sample's metadata says PacBio.

shortread_F.description: Short reads for Pilon polishing only.

report_writer_guidance.purpose: Build an nf-core/genomeassembler sheet from a resolved D.SEQ cohort of long-read libraries.
report_writer_guidance.workflow_role: Selected when the user wants to assemble a genome de novo from ONT or PacBio reads.
report_writer_guidance.output_expectation: CSV with header sample plus whichever platform read column applies.
population_priority: Check the platform in each sample's metadata FIRST. NExtSEEK holds no long-read data today, so expect to have to ask whether the cohort is really ONT or HiFi.
One row per D.SEQ leaf; let the emitter place the read in ontreads or hifireads.
Match the assembler and polisher to the platform: hifiasm for HiFi, medaka polishing for ONT.
final_checks: Every row has a populated read column. A row with all read columns blank means the platform was not recognised — stop and report it rather than launching.
